summary: Row-wise keyed copy of a6 rows, each 2*a5 bytes wide, from source (stride a2) to destination (stride a4). Stores the key word a7 in global dword_5DD804. When a7 is 0xFFFF and the row width is a multiple of 8 it takes a fast block-copy path; otherwise it copies word-by-word and leaves destination words equal to the key unchanged.

operations.description: store the key word a7 into global dword_5DD804
row byte width v10 = 2 * a5; fast path chunks it as 4 * (v10 >> 2) with a (v10 & 3) byte remainder
when a7 == 0xFFFF and (v10 & 7) == 0 take the fast whole-row block-copy path
for each of a6 rows, block-copy v10 bytes from a1 to a3 via 4-byte-dword chunks plus the low-3-bytes tail, then advance source by a2 - v10 and dest by a4 - v10
otherwise fall through to the general per-row path with comparison key v11 = a7 (or 2 * a5 when a7 == 0xFFFF)
for each of a6 rows, scan the source two words at a time; copy each word to the destination only when it differs from the key v11, leaving matching destination words untouched
after each general-path row, advance source pointer by a2 and destination pointer by a4

clean_pseudocode: for (i = 0; i < a6; i++) { block_copy_row(a3, a1, row_bytes); a1 += a2; a3 += a4; }
unresolved: exact purpose of the keyed skip: destination words equal to the key retain prior content (transparency/fill preservation suspected)
why a7 == 0xFFFF substitutes 2*a5 as the comparison key in the general path
